questions.explanation: The useful first step is to state the view in its strongest form. Informed consent requires voluntary, informed, and competent agreement to a procedure. This is the position defended by Tom Beauchamp. The claim that informed consent is a signed form regardless of understanding is a common mistake about the view, often described as "reduces consent to a signature". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: pressure can undermine voluntariness. A careful reader separates the actual doctrine from the frequent misreading.
